# DataKraft

> Clear processes, useful data and practical AI for business teams. Portfolio of working browser demos and practical articles, organised by the kind of team being hired for. Based in Berlin, working in English and German.

Contact: stan.kaylan@gmail.com, sujeet.gorah@gmail.com · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/datakraftai

## Areas
- [AI, Automation & Building](https://datakraftai.github.io/ai-automation/): How I bring AI and automation into real teams: pick the right tasks, build working tools end to end, keep people in control and make sure the tools are actually used. With a working automation finder demo and practical articles.
- [Customer Success, Support & Implementation](https://datakraftai.github.io/customer-success/): How I work with customer success, support and implementation teams: faster first replies, fewer repeat tickets, onboarding that sticks and early churn warnings. With a working ticket triage demo and practical articles.
- [Data & Business Analysis](https://datakraftai.github.io/data-analysis/): How I work as a data or business analyst: start with the decision, check the data, explain findings in plain language and make reports repeatable. With a working data check demo and practical articles.
- [People, Talent & HR](https://datakraftai.github.io/people-talent/): How I work with people and talent teams: structured, fair hiring, a pipeline you can plan, people operations that run smoothly and people data leaders can act on. With a working hiring funnel planner and practical articles.
- [Product Management & Ownership](https://datakraftai.github.io/product/): How I work as a product manager or product owner: discovery, prioritisation, user stories and measurable releases. With a working prioritisation demo and practical articles.
- [Project, Program & Agile Delivery](https://datakraftai.github.io/project-program/): How I run projects and programs: plans in honest ranges, risks seen early, clear ownership and a steady delivery rhythm. With a working delivery forecast demo and practical articles.
- [Sales, Partnerships & Revenue Operations](https://datakraftai.github.io/revenue-gtm/): How I work with sales and revenue teams: clean CRM data, a funnel you can see, less admin for reps and forecasts that hold. With a working pipeline demo and practical articles.
- [Strategy, Operations & Chief of Staff](https://datakraftai.github.io/strategy-ops/): How I work as a chief of staff or in strategy and operations: one version of the numbers, processes that scale, decisions that stick and a clear leadership rhythm. With a working weekly KPI review demo and practical articles.

## Articles
- [Human in the loop: using AI on real work without losing control](https://datakraftai.github.io/ai-automation/human-in-the-loop/): Where people should review AI output, how to make reviewing fast, which cases always go to a person, and what to log, so AI can be used on real work safely.
- [Did the AI tool actually save time? How to measure it honestly](https://datakraftai.github.io/ai-automation/measure-ai-savings/): Many AI tools are declared a success without measurement. How to set a baseline, include review time, track usage and quality, and report savings that leadership can trust.
- [Where to start with AI in operations: boring, frequent and checkable](https://datakraftai.github.io/ai-automation/where-to-start/): How to pick the first AI or automation use case in an operations team: three questions about frequency, checkability and rules, with examples of good and bad first projects.
- [Fewer tickets, not faster agents: fix the top five contact reasons](https://datakraftai.github.io/customer-success/fewer-tickets/): Most support tickets come from a handful of reasons. How to find them in a sample of tickets, fix them at the source and track contact rate instead of only response time.
- [Customer health scores that warn you before a customer leaves](https://datakraftai.github.io/customer-success/health-scores/): Most health scores are too complicated to trust. A simple score from a few behaviour signals, checked against past churn, gives customer success teams an early warning they can act on.
- [A 30-day onboarding plan customers actually finish](https://datakraftai.github.io/customer-success/onboarding-plan/): A simple onboarding structure for B2B customers: one agreed goal, named owners on both sides, a four-week rhythm and an early warning when things stall.
- [Dashboards people actually use: one question per chart](https://datakraftai.github.io/data-analysis/dashboards-people-use/): Why most dashboards are ignored, and five rules for dashboards that end up in every weekly meeting: one question per chart, agreed definitions, comparisons, few charts and a named owner.
- [Start with the decision, not the data](https://datakraftai.github.io/data-analysis/start-with-the-question/): Four questions to ask before opening any spreadsheet: which decision, who decides, by when, and what result would change their mind. How they make analysis faster and more useful.
- [Write the scorecard before the job ad: hiring for outcomes, not wish lists](https://datakraftai.github.io/people-talent/role-scorecards/): A role scorecard defines what a new hire must achieve in year one and what evidence shows they can. Written before the job ad, it makes ads clearer, interviews sharper and decisions fairer.
- [Structured interviews in practice: fairer decisions in less time](https://datakraftai.github.io/people-talent/structured-interviews/): How to run structured interviews: the same questions for every candidate, a rating guide, split responsibilities across interviewers and independent scores before the debrief.
- [From 40 customer complaints to a ranked backlog in one afternoon](https://datakraftai.github.io/product/backlog-from-complaints/): A repeatable method to turn raw customer complaints into a short, ranked product backlog: collect, cluster, count, frame and score.
- [Five questions I ask in every customer interview](https://datakraftai.github.io/product/customer-interviews/): Customer interviews go wrong when they ask about the future. Five questions about past behaviour that reveal real problems, and how to turn the answers into product decisions.
- [User stories developers don't have to rewrite](https://datakraftai.github.io/product/user-stories/): What makes a user story sprint-ready: the INVEST criteria, acceptance criteria that can be tested, a before-and-after example and a pre-refinement checklist.
- [Stop promising dates: forecast delivery with ranges from your own history](https://datakraftai.github.io/project-program/forecast-ranges/): Single delivery dates fail because they ignore variation. A simple simulation using the team's own sprint history gives honest ranges with confidence levels, and better conversations with sponsors.
- [The one-page status report stakeholders actually read](https://datakraftai.github.io/project-program/one-page-status/): A weekly one-page project status: honest red-amber-green rules, the forecast range, the top risks and the decisions needed, in a fixed format that stakeholders can read in two minutes.
- [Why your sales forecast keeps missing, and three CRM rules that fix most of it](https://datakraftai.github.io/revenue-gtm/forecast-rules/): Most forecast misses come from stale close dates, fuzzy stage definitions and missing next steps. Three simple CRM rules and a weekly review fix most of it.
- [Lead routing in an afternoon: faster replies without buying another tool](https://datakraftai.github.io/revenue-gtm/lead-routing/): A practical way to set up lead routing with the CRM and tools you already have: clear rules, a response-time target, a fallback when nobody answers, and one number to track.
- [Win/loss reviews: what lost deals can teach you](https://datakraftai.github.io/revenue-gtm/win-loss-reviews/): Most CRMs record why deals are lost in a dropdown nobody trusts. A simple monthly win/loss review with short buyer conversations gives sales, product and marketing real reasons to act on.
- [Decision memos: how to stop re-opening the same decisions](https://datakraftai.github.io/strategy-ops/decision-memos/): A one-page decision memo format, a simple decision log and one rule that keeps decisions from being re-opened without a new reason.
- [A weekly business review that takes 30 minutes and changes decisions](https://datakraftai.github.io/strategy-ops/weekly-business-review/): How to run a short weekly business review: a handful of agreed KPIs, red items first, decisions before updates, and everything else in writing.

## Notes
- Every area page has a demo that runs entirely in the visitor's browser; no data is sent anywhere.
- Photos: WOCinTech Chat, CC BY 2.0 (https://datakraftai.github.io/credits.html).
